Artificial intelligence is changing the way doctors diagnose diseases, treat patients and manage their workloads. More physicians are using AI than ever before, but questions remain about its accuracy, reliability and impact on patient care.

Coming up at 9 a.m. on Wednesday, MPR News host Angela Davis talks with an expert about how AI is being used in medicine, what’s working well and what researchers are developing next.

As a patient, have you observed your doctor or nurse use AI? What questions do you have about how AI is being used in health care? If you work in health care, how are you using artificial intelligence?

Call us during the 9 a.m. hour at 651-227-6000 or 800-242-2828.

Matt Redlon is chair of the AI program and vice president of digital biology in Mayo Clinic Laboratories’ Digital Pathology initiative. He leads efforts to develop and apply artificial intelligence in medicine, including tools that support disease diagnosis, drug discovery and medical research.
